# DateDiff

Measures the time from one date to another, in a given unit.

## Signature

```jyro
# fragment
DateDiff(startDate, endDate, unit)
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `startDate` | string | The date to measure from: a string in one of the forms `ParseDate` accepts. A string in no accepted form is a runtime error, as is any other type, null included. |
| `endDate` | string | The date to measure to: a string in one of the forms `ParseDate` accepts. A string in no accepted form is a runtime error, as is any other type, null included. |
| `unit` | string | The unit of the result, one of `"day"`, `"days"`, `"week"`, `"weeks"`, `"month"`, `"months"`, `"year"`, `"years"`, `"hour"`, `"hours"`, `"minute"`, `"minutes"`, `"second"` or `"seconds"`, matched with no regard to the case of ASCII letters. Any other string is a runtime error, as is a value that is not a string, null included. |

## Returns

Number. The number of units from startDate to endDate. Never null.

## Remarks

For weeks, days, hours, minutes and seconds the result is the exact elapsed time in that unit and can have a fraction: 36 hours is 1.5 days. For months and years it is a whole number: the largest count n, in magnitude, for which `DateAdd(startDate, n, unit)` does not go past endDate. The result is negative when endDate is before startDate.

## Example

`DateDiff("2024-01-01", "2024-01-15", "days")` returns 14.

`DateDiff("2024-01-31", "2024-03-30", "months")` returns 1.
